routes.title: Healthcare access and hospital care
routes.first: Contact the care team or clinic, then its manager. For SHA services, use the SHA Client Concerns Office; surgical care coordinators can help with surgery navigation.
routes.escalation: Ministry of Health for system access, funding, and policy. For unresolved administrative fairness, check Ombudsman jurisdiction. Professional-conduct concerns may follow a separate regulator process.
routes.note: The provider determines the correct route: not every clinic or screening service is operated by SHA.

routes.title: Childcare access and licensing
routes.first: For a facility concern, contact the caregiver, then the Child Care Regional Office. For access and licensing questions, contact the ministry's Child Care Office.
routes.escalation: Ministry of Education for regulated-childcare capacity, funding, licensing, and access policy. Contacting the ministry does not guarantee a childcare space.

routes.title: School support and complaint handling
routes.ministry: Ministry of Education / local school division
routes.first: Raise the concern with the teacher or principal, then follow the relevant school division's escalation process through senior administration and the board.
routes.escalation: Ministry of Education for provincial funding and policy. The Ombudsman does not investigate schools, teachers, or school boards; ministry administration is a different jurisdiction.
routes.note: The linked Saskatoon Public Schools protocol is one division's example, not a universal provincial procedure.

routes.title: SAID and income assistance
routes.first: Contact the assigned worker or local income-assistance office. Ask for the written decision, reasons, and the review or appeal instructions that apply to that decision.
routes.escalation: Ask for a supervisor review and use the applicable program appeal route. Unresolved administrative fairness concerns can go to Ombudsman Saskatchewan; policy concerns go to Social Services.
routes.note: Appeal rules and deadlines depend on the decision. The program page and decision letter should be checked for a current case.

routes.title: Public-housing conditions
routes.first: Report maintenance and property-management concerns to the local housing authority that manages the property for Saskatchewan Housing Corporation.
routes.escalation: Escalate through the housing authority and Saskatchewan Housing Corporation. Social Services is responsible for housing programs; tenancy disputes may have a separate review route.

routes.title: SaskPower billing and service
routes.first: Contact SaskPower customer service about the account, bill, or meter question. If unresolved, ask for a Customer Services Manager.
routes.escalation: Ombudsman Saskatchewan can review alleged unfairness after the utility has had a chance to respond. CIC provides Crown oversight; it is not the individual account complaint desk.
routes.note: An unexpectedly high bill alone does not establish a meter or billing error.

routes.title: SaskTel service, data, and app issues
routes.first: Contact SaskTel customer service or technical support. Ask for a Customer Services Manager if the concern remains unresolved.
routes.escalation: Eligible unresolved telecom and TV disputes may go to the independent CCTS. Some regulated matters go to CRTC. Provincial utility fairness guidance also identifies the Ombudsman route.
routes.note: CIC oversees the Crown corporation; telecom regulation and CCTS are separate from provincial ministry administration.

routes.title: SGI insurance claim disputes
routes.first: Start with the assigned adjuster and claims supervisor. Ask for the decision and the escalation procedure for the specific SGI CANADA policy or Auto Fund claim.
routes.escalation: Use the applicable insurer review or appeal route. Ombudsman Saskatchewan offers insurance complaint guidance; licensing and no-fault benefit appeals have separate processes.
routes.note: The sampled home-insurance complaint is an SGI CANADA property claim. Do not assume Auto Fund appeal procedures apply to it.

routes.title: Provincial roads and construction signs
routes.first: Use the Highways Customer Service Centre and the inquiry or complaint form on the ministry page. Describe the highway, location, and service concern.
routes.escalation: Ministry of Highways for maintenance, provincial road safety, and construction-signage concerns. Municipal streets and roads should be directed to the responsible municipality.

routes.title: Wildfire response and evacuation support
routes.first: Contact the organization managing the particular assistance file: Saskatchewan Public Safety Agency for its emergency-support program, or the separate relief provider for its services.
routes.escalation: SPSA for operational and support-administration concerns; Community Safety for provincial oversight. Unresolved fairness concerns about a provincial agency can be raised with the Ombudsman.
routes.note: Historical reporting refers to Corrections, Policing and Public Safety; current responsibility is Community Safety. Red Cross is a separate organization. Program eligibility varies by event.
